items.description: EDPS Press Release ✈️ EU-US border information exchange: effective safeguards are essential to protect fundamental rights in practice. A new EDPS Opinion comments on the European Commission’s proposal for a framework agreement between the EU and the US on sharing information to verify, screen and vet travellers. The proposed framework would set common conditions for the reciprocal exchange of data between the authorities of EU Member States and the US for border checks, travel authorisations and visas. The proposal is linked to a US requirement for partner countries in the US Visa Waiver Program to conclude an ‘Enhanced Border Security Partnership’ by the end of 2026. The Opinion sets out the safeguards needed to keep the processing of personal data limited to what is strictly necessary and proportionate. items.title: Welcome to the latest edition of the EDPS Newsletter.
items.description: Welcome to the latest edition of the EDPS Newsletter. Inside: 🎧 Why do cyberattacks start with us? On EDPS on Air, our Technology and Security Officer Konstantina Vemou explains how AI is making phishing harder to spot, and why a once-a-year e-learning module is no longer enough. 🏆 The EDPS receives the Future of Privacy Forum’s 2026 EU Regulator Award for its leadership in safeguarding privacy across the EU institutions. 🤖 Making AI visible: most of the AI Act’s transparency obligations now apply, and EU institutions shared how they’re putting them into practice at the fourth meeting of our AI Act Correspondents Network. 🧭 Weak point, or last line of defence? For European Cybersecurity Month, we look at why well-trained staff are often the best protection, with an updated factsheet on personal data breaches. 🏥 Cross-border health data: our recommendations for the HealthData@EU cross-border infrastructure, so individuals know who to turn to about their personal data. ✈️ What does an airline know about you when you fly to Seoul? items.title: *** Spain Digital Week ***
items.description: *** Spain Digital Week *** Digital humanism as the compass for the AI era. At Spain Digital Week, organised by Adigital at the Permanent Representation of Spain to the EU, the EDPS @ Secretary_General Leonardo Cervera-Navas delivered a speech on the role of the EDPS in a world increasingly governed by AI. He described AI as an amplifier, of both the benefits of digitalisation and its risks, particularly where automated decisions affect people who do not know a machine is involved. “AI amplifies the good brought forth by digitalization allowing for greater efficiency, improved access to services and new opportunities. But it also exacerbates the bad, raising considerable risks as automated decisions are susceptible of profoundly affecting the lives of individuals.” Leonardo Cervera-Navas noted. He explained how the EDPS’s role has evolved: in addition to supervising EU institutions under the EUDPR, the EDPS is now a notified body and market surveillance authority under the AI Act. He presented two initiatives to strengthen coordination across the EU digital rulebook: the AI Act Correspondents Network and the proposed Digital Clearinghouse 2.0.
